sentences.review: The accusative note is attached to "durch das Haus", where the neuter accusative looks the same as the nominative, so the case isn't visible; "Durch dich weiß ich das jetzt" shows it.

meanings.gloss: through, thanks to, by (means or cause)

sentences.text: Durch dich weiß ich das jetzt.
sentences.en: Thanks to you, I know that now.

sentences.text: Er hat sein Geld durch seine Frau.
sentences.en: He got his money through his wife.
sentences.review: "Er hat sein Geld durch seine Frau" is present tense ("has his money through his wife") and sounds odd, while the English uses past tense "got"; consider "Er hat das Geld durch seine Frau" translated in the present, or a clearer cause sentence.

meanings.gloss: through (particle of durchkommen: get through, pull through)
